slots.title: US session recap — Sept. 23, 2026
slots.body:
U.S. equity benchmarks closed lower across the board.
The S&P 500 finished at 7,708.55 (−56.09, −0.7%).
The Nasdaq Composite was weaker at 26,936.04 (−308.24, −1.1%).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended at 51,511.59 (−352.10, −0.7%).
Small caps lagged: the Russell 2000 closed at 2,838.66 (−51.26, −1.8%).

Implied volatility ticked up.
The VIX settled at 15.18, up 0.97 (+6.8%) from the prior close.

Three U.S. S&P Global PMI readings for September were released at 1:45 p.m.
ET with actuals above estimates.
Composite PMI printed 58.4 (estimate 55.2, previous 56.0).
Services PMI was 58.7 (estimate 56.0, previous 56.5).
Manufacturing PMI was 57.0 (estimate 53.6, previous 53.9).

Sector performance on Nasdaq was uneven.
Industrials and real estate led declines, each averaging about −1.8% and −1.8% respectively.
Healthcare averaged about −1.0%.
Technology averaged about −0.8%.
Basic materials was the strongest group, up about +1.1% on average.
Utilities and consumer defensive names were roughly flat to slightly positive.

Megacap technology and internet names mostly closed red.
$GOOG was down 3.6% to 334.98.
$ORCL fell 3.1% to 144.55.
$AMZN lost 2.2% to 249.27.
$AVGO was off 2.6% to 354.99.
$NVDA closed at 225.51 (−1.5%).
$AMD ended at 614.61 (−1.5%).
$TSM finished at 446.57 (−1.2%).
$AAPL closed at 337.02 (−0.8%).
$MSFT bucked the trend, up 0.5% to 500.59.
$CRM gained 1.8% to 237.58.

Energy-linked large caps rose while the Nasdaq energy sector average was still negative.
$XOM closed at 161.28 (+1.6%).
$CVX finished at 205.52 (+1.5%).
The United States Oil Fund ($USO proxy in cross-asset data) closed at 148.83 (+3.3%).
Brent crude in the dataset was 102.09 (−1.0%).

Earnings after the bell window included three names with reported actuals.
Cintas ($CTAS) beat on EPS (1.39 vs 1.35 est.) and revenue (~3.01B vs ~2.98B est.) but the stock closed −3.4% at 191.97.
Paychex ($PAYX) also beat EPS (1.34 vs 1.32) and revenue (~1.63B vs ~1.63B est.) and still fell −8.8% to 104.49.
General Mills ($GIS) beat EPS (0.75 vs 0.717) and revenue (~4.39B vs ~4.35B est.) and closed +1.0% at 35.82.

Cross-asset and rates context from the injected tape: gold futures (GCUSD) settled at 4,326.10 (+0.2%).
The Invesco dollar bull ETF proxy ($UUP) closed at 28.65 (+0.6%).
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was 84,298.20 (−0.1%).
Treasury snapshot dated 2026-09-21 showed the 10-year yield at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.20.

Overseas indexes in the package mixed against the U.S. decline.
The Nikkei 225 closed up 1.3% at 65,883.41.
The Hang Seng was −0.4% at 24,725.94.
The FTSE 100 was essentially unchanged at 10,705.26.

Session narrative in financial press tied equity weakness to bond-market pressure, including coverage of Treasury yield moves and a challenging 5-year note auction weighing on indexes into the close.
